purpose: Evidence-grounded check of the CDM 3.0.3 triples: does the triple's own source sentence state it? Complements the string-only judgement (supplement 04). Rules fixed before the run; this file's sha256 is written to PREREGISTRATION.sha256 first.
items: every triple with a source sentence from a paper whose rights decision is INCLUDE_TEXT (CC BY / CC0); one sentence per triple (first evidence row by triple_mention_id). No text of the 179 withheld papers is sent.

question_per_item.R: Y if the sentence states any relationship between subject and object, else N
question_per_item.A: original relation: Y supported as written; P right entities and relation present but the label is too generic or only partly right; R supported only with subject and object reversed; N not supported
question_per_item.B: cleaned relation and orientation (only when the cleaning changed the label or orientation; otherwise '-'): same codes as A
question_per_item.D: how the sentence states it: F asserted, H hedged or speculative, G negated (the sentence reports no association)

primary: share of triples whose sentence states a relationship between subject and object (R = Y)
share of triples whose original label is supported as written (A = Y)
secondary: A = Y or P (relationship present, label acceptable or generic)
on relabelled triples, paired comparison of A = Y vs B = Y (does the cleaning improve the label?)
A = Y among triples kept vs dropped by the cleaning (Newcombe interval of the difference)
share of triples stated with negation (D = G) while the relation asserts an association

limitations_stated_in_advance: The cleaning (relabelling) was done by the same model family, so the paired comparison A vs B is not independent.
One sentence per triple: a triple stated across sentences can be judged unsupported.
